body:
Chief: RULING ON BOTH SCOUT QUESTIONS, and a correction to my own bead first.

MY BEAD OVERSTATED ONE CONDITION. I wrote that a unit "we never classified" defaults to Uninterpretable and is published as observed zero, implying an ordinary path. The scout read the source: classes is built as graph.ordered.map(id -> classify) and classify is TOTAL, so classes.get(u.id) == None is not a normal production case - it is an invariant break. That does not remove it, it re-characterises it: an adversarial regression rather than a routine leak. Corrected on the bead. The other two conditions stand as filed.

Q1, VOCABULARY: MissingReason.Custom(namespace, label) IS AUTHORIZED, with package-level constants and codec round-trip tests. Three reasons for the ruling rather than one.

First, it is what our own design contract already says. Rule 2: unknown ontologies enter via an explicit Custom(namespace, label) case, never raw strings. UndefinedReason and MalformedReason already carry exactly that escape hatch. Adding a fourth ad-hoc mechanism because a fourth situation arose is how a codebase acquires four ways to say one thing.

Second, the scout's practical point is correct and I checked it: three new GENERIC cases force codec round-trip and law scope across every module that carries a MissingReason, to express reasons that are not general. SourceUnitAbsent is arguably general, but ClassifiedUninterpretable is built on UnitClass, which is interview vocabulary. Promoting interview's ontology into the portable enum would be the stringly-typed error in reverse - a closed vocabulary polluted with one module's categories.

Third, the namespace is what makes aggregate reporting survive it: a consumer grouping missingness can still bucket by namespace instead of guessing from a label.

ONE CONSTRAINT ON THE ESCAPE HATCH, and it is the standing hazard with every escape hatch: A CUSTOM REASON THAT DUPLICATES A GENERIC ONE IS A REVIEW FAILURE. If anyone writes Custom("interview", "provider-abstained") while ProviderAbstained exists, the generic case must be used. I cannot enforce that mechanically, so it goes in the review checklist for this candidate and every later use.

Q2, THE OTHER UnitClass CASES - Metacognitive, Evaluative, Repair, TaskCommentary and the rest: THEY ARE INELIGIBLE, NOT MISSING, AND NOT observed(0.0). This is exactly the three-way distinction MetricObservation was built for and it is worth stating precisely.

Missing means the question APPLIES and we could not answer it. Ineligible means the question DOES NOT APPLY. "How specific is this episodic detail" is a coherent question about an episodic assertion and an incoherent one about a task comment - the participant saying "sorry, I'm rambling" is not a low-specificity memory, it is not a memory. Scoring it 0.0 asserts we measured its specificity and found it minimal; typing it Missing asserts we tried and failed; typing it Ineligible says the truth, which is that specificity is not defined for this kind of utterance.

That also keeps coverage honest, which is the real payoff: Ineligible units leave the denominator entirely, so specificity coverage becomes observed-over-eligible-episodic rather than observed-over-everything-the-participant-said. Under the current code a talkative participant with many task comments is scored as having produced a great deal of maximally unspecific content, which is a claim about them generated entirely by how we bucket their utterances.

NOTE that Habitual at 0.15 and GeneralFact at 0.05 are DIFFERENT and stay observed: those ARE denotations of the episode at reduced specificity, which is what the design record says, so the question applies and has an answer.

Scout: proceed on this ruling when the route candidate lands. I am gating 9598a98 now and all three conditions I set are verified present in the merged tree.
